question: The entrance gateway in Dravidian style temple is known as:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gopuram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A Gopuram is a monumental entrance tower, usually ornate, at the entrance of a Hindu temple, particularly in Southern India.
 
• It is a distinct feature of Dravidian architecture and often richly decorated with sculptures and carvings.
 
• Gopurams are typically adorned with intricate sculptures depicting various deities, mythical creatures, and legends from Hindu mythology.
 
• They serve not just as entrance gateways but also as a prominent architectural focal point of the temple complex.
 
• The height and grandeur of the Gopuram symbolize the temple's importance and are meant to be visible from a distance, guiding devotees to the temple.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shikhara**

 
 
• It is the tower or spire on a Hindu temple, typically found in North Indian temple architecture.
 
• The Shikhara rises above the sanctum where the main deity is enshrined.
 
• It symbolizes the mythical Mount Meru, the axis of the universe in Hindu cosmology.
 
 
 
• **Mandap**
 
 
• It is a pillared hall or pavilion for public rituals in a Hindu temple.
 
• The Mandap is used for religious and ceremonial activities, including weddings and other community gatherings.
 
 
 
• **Vimana**
 
 
• It refers to the tower above the Garbhagriha (sanctum sanctorum) in South Indian temples, similar to the Shikhara in North Indian temples.
 
• The Vimana is usually pyramid-shaped and richly decorated with carvings and sculptures.
 
 
 
• **Dravidian Architecture**
 
 
• A style of architecture that emerged in the southern part of India, characterized by its pyramid-shaped towers and intricate carvings.
 
• It flourished primarily under the rule of the Chola, Chera, and Pandya dynasties.
